result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.transitive_closure()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the transitive closure of a directed graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L19052-L19141){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.transitive_closure() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The transitive closure is a graph where there is an edge `(u, v)` if and only if there is a path from `u` to `v` in the original graph. This is useful for reachability analysis, determining which nodes can reach which other nodes. For example, if there's a path `A -> B -> C` in the original graph, the transitive closure will have edges `A -> B`, `B -> C`, and `A -> C`. This method only works on directed graphs. Undirected graphs should first be converted to directed or analyzed using connectivity methods. Time complexity: `O(V × (V + E))` where `V` is nodes and `E` is edges Space complexity: `O(V + E')` where `E'` is edges in the closure ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : New directed graph representing the transitive closure. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called on an undirected graph. ::: ## Common Use Cases {.doc-common-use-cases} - determining all reachable nodes from a given node - computing transitive dependencies in build systems - checking if one node can influence another in a network - preprocessing for constant-time reachability queries ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The transitive closure is the inverse operation of transitive reduction: ``transitive_closure(transitive_reduction(G)) == transitive_closure(G)`` (for DAGs) ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a simple chain `A -> B -> C`, the transitive closure adds a direct `A -> C` edge to reflect that `A` can reach `C` indirectly: ::: {#66f6cee9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) closure = graph.transitive_closure() # Returns 3 (adds A -> C to the original 2 edges) closure.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: This makes it easy to answer reachability questions in a dependency graph directly from the edge list, without walking the graph each time: ::: {#bfc44804 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="main") .add_node(label="utils") .add_node(label="config") .add_node(label="base") .add_edge("main", "utils") .add_edge("main", "config") .add_edge("utils", "base") .add_edge("config", "base") ) closure = graph.transitive_closure() # "main" now has a direct edge to every module it can reach, including "base" closure.has_edge("main", "base") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: :::
